label: Rosacea
key: Look for persistent **central facial redness** with visible small blood vessels and sometimes acne-like bumps.
describe: A photo typically shows redness and fine vessels across the cheeks and nose, sometimes with papules or pustules.
subject: Dermatology

label: Tinea pedis (athlete’s foot)
key: Recognise **scaling and peeling between the toes** or dry, scaly skin along the soles and sides of the feet.
search: Wikimedia Commons tinea pedis toe webs
describe: A typical photo shows flaky, cracked skin between the toes or diffuse scaling on the sole.
subject: Dermatology

label: Onychomycosis (fungal nail infection)
key: Look for a nail that is **thickened, discoloured, and crumbly**, often beginning at its edge.
describe: A photo typically shows one or more thickened yellow-white nails with rough or crumbly edges.
subject: Dermatology

label: Folliculitis
key: Recognise **small red bumps or pustules centred on hair follicles**.
describe: A typical photo shows clusters of small inflamed bumps, often with a hair visible at the centre.
subject: Dermatology

label: Hidradenitis suppurativa
key: Look for **recurrent deep nodules, abscesses, and scarring** in skin folds such as the armpits or groin.
describe: A photo may show inflamed lumps, drainage openings, and rope-like scars in an armpit or groin.
subject: Dermatology

label: Seborrheic keratosis
key: Recognise a **waxy, sharply edged growth that appears stuck onto the skin**.
search: Wikimedia Commons seborrheic keratosis close up
describe: A typical photo shows a tan-to-brown, slightly raised, waxy-looking lesion with a stuck-on appearance.
subject: Dermatology

label: Actinic keratosis
key: Look for a **rough, sandpaper-like scaly patch** on sun-exposed skin.
describe: A photo typically shows one or more small rough pink or skin-coloured patches on the face, ears, or scalp.
subject: Dermatology

label: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma
key: Recognise a **firm, persistent scaly or crusted growth**, sometimes ulcerated, on sun-exposed skin.
search: Wikimedia Commons cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma
Wikimedia Commons squamous cell carcinoma skin ear
describe: A typical photo shows a raised, rough red lesion or a non-healing crusted sore, often on the face or ear.
subject: Dermatology

label: Dermatofibroma
key: Look for a **small, firm, round pink-brown or brown papule or nodule**, often on a limb; it may dimple inward when compressed from the sides.
describe: A photo typically shows a solitary, round, pink-brown nodule on a limb.
subject: Dermatology

label: Cherry angioma
key: Recognise a **small, bright-red or purple dome-shaped spot** made up of blood vessels.
search: Wikimedia Commons cherry angioma close up
describe: A typical photo shows one or more smooth, round, red spots on the trunk or limbs.
subject: Dermatology

label: Epidermoid cyst
key: Look for a **smooth, rounded lump beneath the skin**, often with a central dark pore.
describe: A photo typically shows a skin-coloured or slightly red dome-shaped lump, sometimes with a visible central opening.
subject: Dermatology

label: Epidermal nevus
key: Look for a **well-defined, often linear or whorled band of thickened bumps** present from birth or early childhood.
describe: A photo typically shows a tan or brown raised, rough plaque following a line or curved pattern on the skin.
subject: Dermatology

label: Perioral dermatitis
key: Recognise **small red bumps around the mouth with a narrow clear margin next to the lips**.
describe: A typical photo shows clusters of small red papules around the mouth, sometimes extending beside the nose or eyes.
subject: Dermatology

label: Hand-foot-and-mouth disease
key: Look for **small blisters or spots on the palms and soles**, often alongside a rash elsewhere.
search: Wikimedia Commons hand foot mouth disease rash
Wikimedia Commons hand foot mouth disease palms
describe: A photo may show scattered small red spots or blisters on the hands and feet, sometimes with lesions around the mouth.
subject: Dermatology

label: Acanthosis nigricans
key: Look for **dark, thickened, velvety skin**, most often in the neck folds or armpits.
describe: A photo typically shows velvety brown or grey thickening across the back of the neck or in an armpit.
subject: Dermatology

label: Erythema multiforme
key: Recognise the distinctive **target-shaped lesions**, often with concentric rings and a darker centre.
describe: A typical photo shows multiple round, three-zone target lesions, often on the backs of the hands or arms.
subject: Dermatology

label: Tinea capitis
key: Look for **patchy hair loss with scale**, sometimes with broken hairs or a scaly, inflamed area.
describe: A photo commonly shows a patchy bald area on the scalp with scaling and short broken hairs.
subject: Dermatology

label: Xanthelasma
key: Identify **soft yellow plaques** near the inner corners of the eyelids.
describe: A typical photo shows flat or slightly raised yellow plaques on the upper or lower eyelids near the nose.
subject: Dermatology

label: Furuncle (boil)
key: Look for a **tender, red, swollen lump** centred on a hair follicle, often with a pus-filled point.
describe: A photo typically shows a solitary inflamed nodule with a central pustule or drainage point.
subject: Dermatology

label: Plaque psoriasis
key: Look for well-demarcated, raised **red plaques** covered by **silvery-white scale**.
describe: A typical photo shows sharply defined scaly plaques, often on the elbows, knees, or scalp.
subject: General medicine

label: Vitiligo
key: Recognise sharply bordered patches of **depigmented white skin**.
describe: A typical photo shows pale patches on the face, hands, or other areas of skin.
subject: General medicine

label: Acne vulgaris
key: Look for a mixture of **comedones**, inflamed papules, pustules, or nodules on acne-prone skin.
describe: A typical photo shows spots and comedones on the face, chest, or back.
subject: General medicine

label: Rosacea
key: Recognise persistent central facial **redness** with visible **telangiectasia**, sometimes with papules or pustules.
describe: A typical photo shows redness across the cheeks and nose, sometimes with small inflamed bumps.
subject: General medicine

label: Herpes zoster (shingles)
key: Look for grouped **vesicles** in a painful-looking band that usually follows one side of a dermatome.
describe: A typical photo shows clustered blisters in a one-sided strip that does not cross the midline.
subject: General medicine

label: Erythema nodosum
key: Recognise multiple tender-looking **red nodules** over the fronts of the lower legs.
describe: A typical photo shows raised red or bruise-like nodules on both shins.
subject: General medicine

label: Tinea corporis (ringworm)
key: Look for an **annular**, scaly lesion with a more active outer edge and relative central clearing.
describe: A typical photo shows one or more ring-shaped, scaly patches on the skin.
subject: General medicine

label: Atopic dermatitis (eczema)
key: Recognise dry, inflamed, often excoriated patches; chronic lesions may show skin thickening and accentuated skin markings.
describe: A typical photo shows dry, red, sometimes excoriated patches, commonly in the elbow or knee creases.
subject: General medicine

label: Seborrhoeic dermatitis
key: Look for **greasy scale** and redness in areas such as the scalp, eyebrows, sides of the nose, or ears.
describe: A typical photo shows flaky scalp or scale and redness around the eyebrows and nose.
subject: General medicine

label: Urticaria (hives)
key: Recognise raised, smooth **wheals** with variable shapes that may merge and change location.
describe: A typical photo shows scattered or confluent raised wheals on the skin.
subject: General medicine

label: Cellulitis
key: Look for a poorly defined area of **redness** and **swelling**, usually affecting one limb; warmth is a clinical feature but cannot be assessed from a photo.
describe: A typical photo shows one limb with a visibly red, swollen patch of skin.
subject: General medicine

label: Varicose veins
key: Recognise enlarged, tortuous, **superficial veins**, usually on the legs.
describe: A typical photo shows prominent, winding blue or purple veins on the lower leg.
subject: General medicine

label: Venous stasis dermatitis
key: Look for lower-leg **brown discoloration** with scaly, inflamed skin, often around the ankles.
describe: A typical photo shows discoloured, dry or inflamed skin around the lower leg and ankle.
subject: General medicine

label: Dupuytren contracture
key: Recognise a firm **palmar cord** that pulls one or more fingers into flexion.
describe: A typical photo shows a thickened palm and a finger, often the ring finger, bent toward the palm.
subject: General medicine

label: Oral candidiasis (thrush)
key: Look for **creamy white plaques** on the tongue or oral mucosa that can usually be wiped or scraped away, often leaving an erythematous surface.
describe: A typical photo shows creamy white patches on the tongue or inside the mouth.
subject: General medicine

label: Bell palsy
key: Look for **one-sided facial weakness**, including a drooping mouth and inability to fully close the eye on that side.
search: facial nerve palsy face Wikimedia Commons
describe: A typical photo shows asymmetric facial movement, often with one corner of the mouth drooping.
subject: General medicine

label: Acromegaly
key: Recognise **coarsened facial features**, especially an enlarged jaw, broad nose, and thickened lips.
describe: A typical photo shows a broad, prominent lower face and enlarged facial features.
subject: General medicine

label: Heberden nodes of osteoarthritis
key: Look for **bony enlargements at the distal finger joints**, near the fingertips.
describe: A typical photo shows firm-looking bumps at the end joints of one or more fingers.
subject: General medicine

label: Impetigo
key: The characteristic clue is **golden, honey-coloured crusting**, often around the nose or mouth.
describe: A typical photo shows superficial red sores with yellow-brown crusts on the face or limbs.
subject: General medicine

label: Molluscum contagiosum
key: Recognise **small, smooth, pearly bumps with a central dimple**.
describe: A typical photo shows a cluster of small dome-shaped skin-coloured or pink papules with central indentations.
subject: General medicine

label: Scabies
key: Look for **thin, winding burrows and itchy papules**, often between the fingers or at the wrists.
describe: A typical photo shows small itchy bumps and fine burrow lines on the hands or wrists.
subject: General medicine

label: Tinea pedis (athlete's foot)
key: The visible clue is **scaling and cracking between the toes** or along the sole.
search: tinea pedis between toes Wikimedia Commons
describe: A typical photo shows flaky, whitish or reddened skin in the toe webs, sometimes with fissures.
subject: General medicine

label: Onychomycosis (fungal nail infection)
key: Look for **thickened, discoloured, brittle nails**, often with crumbly material beneath the nail.
describe: A typical photo shows a toenail that is yellow-white, thickened, and irregular at the edge.
subject: General medicine

label: Erythema migrans of Lyme disease
key: Recognise an **expanding red patch**, sometimes with central clearing, at the site of a tick bite.
describe: A typical photo shows a gradually enlarging round or oval red patch on the skin.
subject: General medicine

label: Herpes labialis (cold sores)
key: The characteristic feature is **grouped fluid-filled blisters** at the lip edge that may crust over.
describe: A typical photo shows a cluster of small blisters or crusted sores at the border of the lip.
subject: General medicine

label: Aphthous ulcer (canker sore)
key: Look for a **shallow, round ulcer with a pale centre and red rim** on the inside of the mouth.
describe: A typical photo shows a small, round sore on the inner lip, cheek, or tongue.
subject: General medicine

label: Oral leukoplakia
key: Recognise a **persistent white patch in the mouth that does not wipe away**.
describe: A typical photo shows a well-defined white patch on the tongue or inner cheek.
subject: General medicine

label: Acute conjunctivitis
key: The key visible sign is **diffuse redness of the white of the eye**, often with discharge or watery tearing.
describe: A typical photo shows a red, irritated eye with watery or sticky discharge.
subject: General medicine

label: Hordeolum (stye)
key: Look for a **tender, red lump at the eyelid margin**, sometimes with a small pustule.
describe: A typical photo shows a localised swollen red bump on the upper or lower eyelid.
subject: General medicine

label: Parotid gland enlargement
key: Recognise **swelling in front of and below the ear**, which can obscure the angle of the jaw.
describe: A typical photo shows fullness over the cheek just in front of the ear, sometimes on both sides.
subject: General medicine

label: Angular cheilitis
key: Look for **redness, cracking, or crusting at one or both corners of the mouth**.
describe: A typical photo shows irritated, fissured skin at the corner of the mouth, sometimes with a small crust.
subject: General medicine

label: Blepharitis
key: Look for **red, crusted eyelid margins** with flakes or debris around the eyelashes.
describe: A close-up typically shows red eyelid edges with crusting or flakes at the lash roots.
subject: Eye

label: Ectropion
key: The **lower eyelid turns outward**, often exposing its inner surface and leaving the eye watery.
describe: The lower lid droops away from the eyeball, revealing pink inner lid tissue.
subject: Eye

label: Entropion
key: The **eyelid turns inward**, so the eyelashes point toward and may touch the eye.
describe: The lid margin rolls inward, with lashes visibly directed toward the eyeball.
subject: Eye

label: Trichiasis
key: One or more **misdirected eyelashes rub against the eye** instead of pointing outward.
describe: A close-up shows lashes turning inward and contacting the eye surface.
subject: Eye

label: Xanthelasma
key: Recognise **soft yellow plaques** on or near the inner parts of the eyelids.
describe: One or more flat, yellowish plaques are visible near the inner corners of the eyelids.
subject: Eye

label: Pinguecula
key: Look for a **small yellow-white raised patch** on the conjunctiva beside the cornea.
describe: A yellowish bump sits on the white of the eye, usually on the side nearest the nose.
subject: Eye

label: Corneal arcus
key: A **pale grey-white ring at the edge of the cornea** is the characteristic feature.
describe: A light-coloured arc or ring outlines the outer edge of the cornea.
subject: Eye

label: Episcleritis
key: The eye has a **sector of superficial redness**, often bright red and sharply localised.
describe: A patch of redness appears on the white of the eye, often without extensive swelling.
subject: Eye

label: Scleritis
key: Look for **deep, diffuse redness** of the white of the eye, often with a dusky or violaceous hue.
describe: The eye appears markedly and deeply red, sometimes with a purple-blue tint.
subject: Eye

label: Hyphema
key: A **visible layer or pool of blood in front of the iris** is the key finding.
describe: Blood collects in the lower part of the front of the eye, behind the clear cornea.
subject: Eye

label: Hypopyon
key: A **white or yellow fluid level in front of the iris** settles at the bottom of the eye.
describe: A pale, horizontal collection is visible in the lower front chamber of the eye.
subject: Eye

label: Thyroid eye disease
key: Recognise **prominent, staring eyes** with upper-lid retraction and a wide-eyed appearance.
describe: The eyes may protrude, with retracted upper lids and increased white visible above the iris.
subject: Eye

label: Anterior uveitis
key: Look for **redness concentrated around the cornea** with a small or irregular pupil.
describe: The eye shows a red ring around the cornea, and the pupil may look constricted or irregular.
subject: Eye

label: Dacryocystitis
key: A **red, tender-looking swelling below the inner corner of the eye** overlies the tear sac.
describe: A localised red swelling is visible beside the nose, just below the inner corner of the eye.
subject: Eye

label: Corneal scar
key: A **fixed white or grey opacity on the clear cornea** distinguishes a scar from a clear cornea.
describe: A white or grey mark is visible on the normally transparent front surface of the eye.
subject: Eye

label: Orbital cellulitis
key: Look for **one-sided eyelid swelling and redness with a protruding eye**, often with restricted eye movement.
describe: A swollen, red eyelid surrounds a visibly protruding eye, sometimes with the eye turned or movement limited.
subject: Eye

label: Herpes zoster ophthalmicus
key: Recognise **grouped blisters in the forehead and upper eyelid** on one side, usually following the ophthalmic branch of the trigeminal nerve.
describe: A one-sided band of crusted or fluid-filled blisters covers the forehead and may involve the upper eyelid.
subject: Eye

label: Eyelid molluscum contagiosum
key: The characteristic lesion is a small, smooth, dome-shaped papule with a central **umbilication** on the eyelid.
describe: A pearly, rounded eyelid bump has a tiny central dimple.
subject: Eye

label: Conjunctival nevus
key: Look for a **well-defined, flat or slightly raised pigmented spot** on the visible white of the eye, often with small cysts.
describe: A sharply bordered brown spot sits on the conjunctiva, often near the edge of the cornea.
subject: Eye

label: Conjunctival melanoma
key: A suspicious lesion is a **raised, irregularly pigmented conjunctival mass**, sometimes with prominent feeding vessels.
describe: An uneven dark patch or nodule on the eye surface has visible blood vessels.
subject: Eye

label: Iris coloboma
key: The pupil has a keyhole appearance because of a **downward notch in the iris**.
describe: The normally round pupil extends downward through a gap in the iris.
subject: Eye

label: Aniridia
key: Recognise a **markedly absent or underdeveloped iris**, leaving an unusually large, exposed-looking pupil.
describe: Both eyes may show very large dark pupils with little visible iris.
subject: Eye

label: Heterochromia iridis
key: The defining feature is **different iris colours** between the two eyes or distinct colour zones within one iris.
describe: The two irises are visibly different colours, or one iris contains contrasting colour sectors.
subject: Eye

label: Esotropia
key: One eye turns **inward toward the nose** while the other eye looks straight ahead or in another direction.
describe: In a forward-looking face, one eye is visibly deviated toward the nose.
subject: Eye

label: Exotropia
key: One eye turns **outward toward the temple** rather than aligning with the other eye.
describe: One eye points outward while the other is directed forward.
subject: Eye

label: Keratoconus
key: In advanced cases, look for **Munson sign: a V-shaped bulge of the lower eyelid on downward gaze**.
describe: On downward gaze, the lower eyelid may form a V-shaped bulge over the steep, cone-shaped cornea.
subject: Eye

label: Congenital glaucoma
key: Look for an unusually **enlarged eye with a cloudy cornea**, especially in an infant.
describe: An infant’s eye appears enlarged and the normally clear cornea looks hazy.
subject: Eye

label: Retinoblastoma presenting with leukocoria
key: A key warning sign is **white rather than red pupil reflection** in a child, particularly when seen in photographs.
describe: One pupil shows a white reflection instead of the usual red-eye reflection in a flash photograph.
subject: Eye

label: Facial nerve palsy with lagophthalmos
key: The affected eye does not close fully, leaving a visible **gap between the eyelids** when the patient attempts to shut it.
describe: On attempted eye closure, the eyelids remain partly open on the affected side.
subject: Eye

label: Limbal dermoid
key: Recognise a **pale, raised, rounded lesion at the corneal edge**, often present from birth.
describe: A cream-coloured lump straddles the border between the clear cornea and the white of the eye.
subject: Eye

label: Preseptal cellulitis
key: Look for **redness and swelling of one eyelid**, with the eye itself usually not pushed forward.
describe: A swollen, red eyelid surrounds an eye that remains in its usual position.
subject: Eye

label: Conjunctival chemosis
key: The conjunctiva appears as **soft, balloon-like swelling**, often bulging around the edge of the cornea.
describe: Clear or pink, fluid-filled conjunctiva protrudes around the eyeball.
subject: Eye

label: Proptosis
key: Recognise an eye that **protrudes forward compared with the other eye or the surrounding orbital structures**; the eyelids may be unable to close fully.
describe: One or both eyeballs project forward compared with the surrounding orbital structures.
subject: Eye

label: Dermatochalasis
key: Look for **loose, excess upper-eyelid skin** that hangs over the lid crease and may partly obscure the eye.
describe: Redundant folds of upper-eyelid skin drape over the eyelid.
subject: Eye

label: Eyelid basal cell carcinoma
key: A **pearly or shiny eyelid nodule with a rolled edge**, visible fine blood vessels, or loss of nearby eyelashes is suspicious.
search: eyelid basal cell carcinoma Wikimedia Commons
basal cell carcinoma eyelid rolled edge
describe: A pearly nodule or ulcer sits on the eyelid, often near the lower lid or inner corner.
subject: Eye

label: Eyelid papilloma
key: Identify a **small, raised, skin-coloured or pigmented growth** on the eyelid, sometimes with a frond-like surface.
describe: A discrete, soft-looking growth projects from the eyelid skin or margin.
subject: Eye

label: Corneal foreign body
key: Look for a **tiny speck on the corneal surface**, sometimes surrounded by a local white ring or redness.
search: metallic corneal foreign body Wikimedia Commons
describe: A small dark or metallic particle is visibly lodged on the cornea.
subject: Eye

label: Phthisis bulbi
key: The affected eye is **shrunken and disorganised**, often with an irregular pupil or cloudy surface.
search: shrunken eye phthisis bulbi Wikimedia Commons
describe: A markedly small, misshapen eye contrasts with the normal fellow eye.
subject: Eye

label: Anisocoria
key: Compare the pupils: **one is visibly larger than the other** under the same lighting conditions.
describe: The two pupils are clearly different in diameter.
subject: Eye

label: Ocular surface squamous neoplasia
key: Look for a **raised, gelatinous or irregular white-red lesion** at the limbus, the boundary between cornea and sclera.
search: ocular surface squamous neoplasia Wikimedia Commons
conjunctival squamous neoplasia limbus Wikimedia Commons
describe: A fleshy, irregular lesion extends across the conjunctiva near the corneal edge.
subject: Eye

label: Conjunctival cyst
key: Recognise a **smooth, translucent, fluid-filled bubble** on the conjunctiva, distinct from diffuse swelling.
search: conjunctival inclusion cyst eye Wikimedia Commons
describe: A clear, rounded bubble sits on the white of the eye or inside the eyelid.
subject: Eye

label: Herpes labialis
key: Grouped **painful blisters and crusts** at the lip border are characteristic.
describe: A cluster of small blisters or crusted sores appears on the lip border.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Oral lichen planus
key: Fine white **lacy lines (Wickham striae)** on the inner cheek are a classic clue.
describe: Lacy white lines form a network on the inner cheek, sometimes with red or ulcerated areas.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Oral erythroplakia
key: A persistent, sharply defined **velvety red patch** on the oral mucosa is the key appearance.
describe: A distinct red patch is visible on the tongue, floor of the mouth, or inner cheek.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Oral squamous cell carcinoma
key: A persistent, non-healing ulcer or irregular oral mass is a concerning visual feature; it may have a rolled or irregular edge.
describe: An irregular ulcer or growth is seen on the tongue or another part of the mouth.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Oral mucocele
key: A smooth, dome-shaped **bluish or translucent swelling**, often on the lower lip, is typical.
describe: A soft-looking, rounded blue or clear bump sits on the inner lower lip.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Ranula
key: A **bluish, fluctuant swelling** in the floor of the mouth is the characteristic finding.
describe: A smooth, often blue-tinged swelling bulges beneath the tongue.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Median rhomboid glossitis
key: A smooth, red, **midline patch on the back of the tongue** is the key feature.
describe: A well-defined red, smooth area is visible in the middle of the posterior tongue.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Black hairy tongue
key: Elongated papillae create a **dark, hair-like coating** on the upper surface of the tongue.
describe: The tongue dorsum has a dark coating with a furry or hairy appearance.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Oral irritation fibroma
key: A smooth, firm-looking **mucosa-coloured nodule** is a typical appearance.
describe: A round, smooth, pink-coloured lump is visible, often along the inner cheek or lip.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Gingival pyogenic granuloma
key: A bright red, friable, often lobulated growth on the gum is characteristic.
describe: A red, lobulated gum growth protrudes between or beside the teeth.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Dental caries
key: Visible **cavitations or darkened defects** in the tooth surface are typical clues.
describe: One or more teeth show brown or black areas, pits, or obvious cavities.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Dental fluorosis
key: Diffuse **white flecks or mottling** across multiple teeth are a characteristic pattern.
describe: Several teeth show symmetrical white streaks or mottled enamel.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Nasal polyps
key: Smooth, pale, **grape-like masses** visible in the nasal passage suggest nasal polyps.
describe: Pale, smooth masses are seen within one or both nostrils during examination.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Deviated nasal septum
key: A visibly **off-centre septum** narrowing one nasal passage is the key finding.
describe: The septum is visibly displaced to one side when the nostrils are examined.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Rhinophyma
key: A **bulbous, thickened nose with enlarged pores** is characteristic.
describe: The nose appears enlarged and irregular, with thickened skin and prominent pores.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Gingivitis
key: The gums are **red, swollen, and bleed easily**, especially along the tooth margins.
describe: A clinical mouth photo shows inflamed red gums around several teeth, sometimes with bleeding.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Periodontitis
key: Look for **gum recession, visible root exposure, and loss of support around teeth**; plaque or calculus may also be present. Deepened periodontal pockets cannot be reliably identified from a photo alone.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Denture stomatitis
key: The tissue beneath an upper denture is **diffusely red**, sometimes with pinpoint red areas; the redness may correspond to the denture-bearing area.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Oral squamous papilloma
key: This usually benign growth has a **small, papillary or cauliflower-like surface** on a stalk or broad base.
describe: A small pale or pink finger-like growth projects from the oral lining.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Fordyce spots
key: These normal visible sebaceous glands appear as **multiple tiny yellow-white spots** on the inner lips or cheeks.
search: Fordyce granules oral mucosa Wikimedia Commons
describe: Close-up of the inner lip or cheek shows scattered, pale-yellow pinhead-sized spots.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Torus palatinus
key: A **hard, midline bony lump** rises from the roof of the mouth and is covered by normal-looking mucosa.
search: palatal torus clinical photo Wikimedia Commons
describe: The palate shows a smooth, firm-looking central bony prominence.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Ankyloglossia
key: A **short, tight lingual frenulum** visibly tethers the tongue and limits its elevation or protrusion.
search: tongue tie clinical photo Wikimedia Commons
describe: With the tongue lifted, a tight band beneath it restricts movement.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Leukoedema
key: The cheek lining has a **diffuse, milky-white, slightly wrinkled appearance** that fades when stretched.
search: leukoedema buccal mucosa photo Wikimedia Commons
describe: A cheek retractor exposes a pale, opalescent inner cheek with fine folds.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Linea alba of the cheek
key: A **thin white horizontal line** runs along the inner cheek at the level where the teeth meet.
search: linea alba buccal mucosa Wikimedia Commons
linea alba cheek oral photo Wikimedia Commons
describe: A close-up of the cheek shows a narrow white line corresponding to the bite line.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Traumatic oral ulcer
key: A **solitary shallow ulcer with a yellow-white base and red rim** lies where it may contact a sharp tooth or appliance.
search: traumatic mouth ulcer clinical photo Wikimedia Commons
describe: A single sore with a pale center and inflamed border appears beside a tooth or denture.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Gingival recession
key: The gum margin has moved **away from the crown, exposing part of the tooth root**.
search: receding gums clinical photo Wikimedia Commons
describe: One or more teeth look unusually long because the gumline is lower than expected.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Cerumen impaction
key: A **plug of earwax obstructs the external ear canal**, partly or completely hiding the eardrum.
describe: An otoscopic view shows a wax plug filling the ear canal.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Acute otitis media
key: The eardrum appears **bulging and opaque**, with landmarks obscured and sometimes redness or fluid behind it.
search: acute otitis media otoscopy Wikimedia Commons
describe: An otoscopic photo shows a full, cloudy eardrum that bulges into the canal.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Auricular hematoma
key: A **soft-looking, swollen collection over the outer ear cartilage** distorts the usual folds, often after trauma.
search: pinna hematoma clinical photo Wikimedia Commons
describe: The outer ear has a localized rounded swelling that obscures its normal contours.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Cauliflower ear
key: The pinna has **thickened, irregular scarred contours** from prior cartilage injury.
search: cauliflower ear clinical photo Wikimedia Commons
describe: The outer ear appears permanently lumpy and distorted, with flattened normal folds.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Hand, foot and mouth disease
key: Recognise **small mouth blisters or ulcers** alongside a rash of spots or blisters on the palms and soles.
describe: Small oral sores, often with spots or blisters visible on the hands or feet.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Herpangina
key: Look for **small blisters or ulcers at the back of the mouth**, especially on the soft palate and around the tonsils.
describe: Several small red-rimmed sores clustered toward the back of the mouth.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Primary herpetic gingivostomatitis
key: The combination of **widespread painful mouth sores** and **bright-red, swollen gums** is characteristic.
describe: Inflamed gums with multiple small ulcers or blisters across the mouth and lips.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Macroglossia
key: Identify a **larger-than-usual tongue** that may protrude beyond the teeth or show tooth impressions along its edges.
describe: An enlarged tongue, sometimes extending outside the mouth or bearing scalloped tooth marks.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Fissured tongue
key: Recognise **prominent grooves or cracks** running across the surface of the tongue.
describe: A tongue with visible grooves of varying depth across its upper surface.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Acute parotitis
key: Look for **swelling in front of and below the ear**, which can blur the jaw angle on the affected side.
describe: Visible cheek swelling extending from the area in front of the ear toward the angle of the jaw.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Allergic rhinitis
key: Typical visible clues include **pale, swollen nasal lining** and, on the face, an **allergic nasal crease** from repeated upward rubbing.
describe: Pale, puffy tissue inside the nostrils, sometimes accompanied by a horizontal crease across the nose.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Nasal vestibulitis
key: Recognise **redness, crusting, or small sores just inside the nostril** at the entrance of the nose.
describe: An irritated nostril entrance with redness and sometimes crusts or a small tender-looking sore.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Preauricular sinus
key: Look for a **tiny pit or opening just in front of the upper ear**, often present from birth.
describe: A small, pinpoint opening in the skin immediately in front of the ear.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Earlobe keloid
key: Identify a **firm, raised scar that grows beyond the original piercing or injury site** on the earlobe.
describe: A smooth, raised lump of scar tissue on an earlobe, often around a piercing.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Tonsillolith (tonsil stone)
key: Look for **white or yellow plugs** lodged in the **tonsillar crypts**.
describe: A typical photo shows one or more pale, firm-looking deposits within the surface pits of a tonsil.
subject: ENT & mouth

label: Impetigo
key: Look for **honey-coloured crusts** over superficial sores, often around the nose and mouth.
describe: A child with small facial sores covered by golden crusts.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Atopic dermatitis (eczema)
key: Recognise **dry, itchy, inflamed patches**, often on the cheeks or in the creases of the elbows and knees.
describe: A child with red, dry, scaly patches on the face or flexural skin.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Scabies
key: Look for **intensely itchy papules and burrows**, especially between the fingers and on the wrists.
describe: Small itchy bumps and fine tracks on a child's hands or wrists.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Molluscum contagiosum
key: Identify **small, pearly, dome-shaped bumps with a central dimple**.
describe: A cluster of smooth, skin-coloured or pink bumps, often on the trunk or limbs.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Tinea capitis
key: Recognise **scaly patches of scalp with broken hairs or hair loss**.
describe: A child with one or more scaly areas of hair loss on the scalp.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Alopecia areata
key: Look for **smooth, sharply defined patches of hair loss** without visible scaling.
describe: A round or oval bald patch on a child's scalp with otherwise normal-looking skin.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Infantile haemangioma
key: Identify a raised or flat **bright-red vascular mark** that may have a lobulated, strawberry-like surface.
describe: A well-defined red mark or raised lesion on an infant's skin.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Café-au-lait macules
key: Recognise **flat, evenly pigmented light-brown patches** with smooth, well-defined borders.
search: Wikimedia Commons cafe au lait macules child
describe: Several flat, light-brown patches visible on a child's skin.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Congenital dermal melanocytosis
key: Look for **blue-grey, flat patches**, usually over the lower back or buttocks.
search: Wikimedia Commons congenital dermal melanocytosis infant
describe: A blue-grey patch over an infant's lower back or buttocks.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Port-wine stain
key: Identify a **flat, persistent pink-to-purple birthmark** with sharply defined edges.
search: Wikimedia Commons port wine stain child
describe: A pink, red, or purple patch, often covering part of a child's face.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Infantile seborrhoeic dermatitis (cradle cap)
key: Recognise **greasy yellow scales** on the scalp, sometimes extending to the eyebrows or skin folds.
describe: Yellow, greasy scales adhering to an infant's scalp.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Oral candidiasis (thrush)
key: Look for **white plaques on the tongue or inner cheeks** that do not wipe away easily.
describe: White patches on an infant's tongue or inner cheek.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Congenital talipes equinovarus (clubfoot)
key: Recognise a foot turned **downwards and inwards**, with the sole rotated towards the other foot.
describe: A newborn's foot visibly turned inward and downward.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Polydactyly
key: Identify **an extra digit** on a hand or foot.
describe: A newborn's hand or foot with an additional finger or toe.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Umbilical hernia
key: Look for a **soft bulge at the umbilicus**, especially when the infant cries or strains.
describe: A rounded protrusion at an infant's navel.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Erythema toxicum neonatorum
key: Look for scattered **red blotches with tiny central papules or pustules** on a well newborn, often sparing the palms and soles.
describe: A newborn has scattered red patches with small pale or yellowish bumps, especially on the trunk.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Neonatal milia
key: Recognise the **tiny, firm white or yellow bumps** clustered mainly on a newborn’s nose and cheeks.
describe: A newborn’s nose and cheeks show numerous pinhead-sized white bumps.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Neonatal acne
key: Look for small red papules and pustules, usually on an infant’s cheeks, forehead, or chin; comedones are absent.
describe: An infant has scattered red bumps, sometimes with small pustules, on the face.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Erythema infectiosum (fifth disease)
key: The characteristic clue is **bright red cheeks**, sometimes followed by a lacy rash on the limbs.
describe: A child has strikingly red cheeks, with or without a faint net-like rash on the arms.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Scarlet fever
key: Recognise the **fine, rough, sandpaper-like red rash**, often with flushed cheeks and a pale area around the mouth.
describe: A child has a widespread fine red rash that looks and feels like sandpaper.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Viral warts (verruca vulgaris)
key: Look for **firm, rough-surfaced papules**, often on the fingers, hands, or knees.
describe: One or more raised, rough bumps are visible on a child’s hand or finger.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Pityriasis alba
key: The key feature is **pale, poorly defined patches with fine surface scale**, commonly on a child’s face.
describe: A child has faint, lighter patches with slightly dry or scaly surfaces on the cheeks.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Vitiligo
key: Recognise **sharply demarcated, milk-white patches** that contrast clearly with the surrounding skin.
describe: Distinct white patches are visible on the face, hands, or other areas of skin.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Plaque psoriasis
key: Look for **well-defined red plaques with silvery scale**, often on the elbows, knees, or scalp.
describe: A child has sharply outlined, scaly plaques on an extensor surface or the scalp.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Congenital muscular torticollis
key: The visible clue is a **persistent head tilt with the chin turned toward the opposite side**.
describe: An infant holds the head tilted to one side, with the face turned away from it.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Positional plagiocephaly
key: Look for **asymmetrical flattening of the back or side of the skull**, sometimes with a forward-shifted ear.
describe: The infant’s head appears uneven from above, with flattening on one side of the back of the skull.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Umbilical granuloma
key: Recognise a **small, moist, pink-red lump** in the umbilicus after the cord has fallen off.
describe: A small, moist pink growth is visible at the base of an infant’s belly button.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Genu varum (bow legs)
key: The key feature is **outward bowing of the legs** when the child stands with the feet together.
describe: A standing toddler’s knees remain apart when the ankles are brought together.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Genu valgum (knock knees)
key: Look for **knees angling inward and touching** while the ankles remain separated.
describe: A standing child’s knees meet while a visible gap remains between the ankles.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Nutritional rickets
key: Visible clues can include **bowed legs** and **prominent widening at the wrists or ankles**.
describe: A child may show bowed legs together with visibly widened wrists or ankles.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Head lice (pediculosis capitis)
key: Look for **nits firmly attached to hair shafts**, especially behind the ears and at the nape of the neck.
describe: A close-up of a child’s scalp and hair showing small oval nits attached near the roots.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Bacterial conjunctivitis
key: The eye is **red with mucopurulent discharge** that may crust the eyelids together.
describe: A close-up showing a red conjunctiva and yellowish discharge along the eyelid.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Strabismus
key: The eyes are **misaligned**, with one eye appearing to turn inward, outward, upward, or downward.
describe: A front-facing portrait in which the two eyes are visibly not directed at the same point.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Congenital ptosis
key: A **drooping upper eyelid** partially covers the eye, sometimes obscuring the pupil.
describe: A child’s face showing one upper eyelid sitting noticeably lower than the other.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Early childhood dental caries
key: Look for **cavitated or discoloured areas on the teeth**, often affecting the upper front teeth in young children.
describe: An open-mouth view showing decayed, discoloured primary teeth.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Herpes labialis
key: Grouped **small blisters or crusted erosions at the lip margin** are characteristic.
describe: A close-up of the lips showing a cluster of vesicles or crusts at the border of the lip.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Erythema multiforme
key: The hallmark is a **target-shaped lesion** with concentric rings of different colour.
describe: A skin close-up showing round lesions with darker centres and pale and red outer rings.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Keratosis pilaris
key: Numerous tiny **rough follicular bumps**, often on the upper arms or cheeks, give the skin a sandpaper-like texture.
describe: A close-up of the upper arm showing many small, rough, skin-coloured or reddish bumps.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Papular urticaria
key: Look for **itchy clusters of papules**, often with a central punctum and on exposed areas of skin.
describe: A skin view showing grouped raised red bumps, sometimes with small central marks.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Nevus simplex (salmon patch)
key: This is a **flat, pale pink-red patch** commonly seen on the eyelids, forehead, or nape of the neck.
describe: A newborn’s face or nape showing a flat, faint pink-red patch.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Cephalohematoma
key: A well-defined scalp swelling that does not cross cranial suture lines is the key visible feature.
describe: A newborn’s scalp with a localized, rounded swelling over one skull bone.
subject: Paediatrics

label: Umbilical hernia
key: Look for a **soft bulge at the umbilicus** that becomes more prominent with coughing or straining.
describe: A rounded protrusion centered on the navel, sometimes with stretched or everted skin.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Incisional hernia
key: Recognise a **bulge through a previous surgical scar**, often more obvious when the patient stands or strains.
describe: A localized swelling protrudes along an old abdominal incision.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Spermatic cord hydrocele
key: Look for a **smooth, cystic swelling along the spermatic cord**, separate from the testis and typically above the scrotum.
describe: A discrete, rounded groin or upper-scrotal swelling along the cord.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Varicocele
key: Recognise **dilated, tortuous veins above the testis**, classically described as a bag of worms.
describe: A cluster of soft, winding veins visible or palpable above a testis.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Phimosis
key: Identify a **tight foreskin that cannot be retracted** over the glans.
describe: The narrowed foreskin opening remains in front of and obscures the glans.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Paraphimosis
key: Look for a **retracted foreskin trapped behind the glans**, producing a swollen constriction ring.
describe: The glans is exposed and swollen, with a tight band of foreskin behind it.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Pilonidal sinus
key: Recognise **midline pits in the natal cleft**, sometimes with surrounding inflamed tissue or draining openings.
describe: One or more small pits or openings are visible in the cleft between the buttocks.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Anal fissure
key: Look for a **linear tear in the anoderm**, usually at the posterior midline.
describe: A narrow midline split at the anal verge, sometimes with a small sentinel skin tag.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: External haemorrhoids
key: Identify **swollen bluish perianal lumps**, especially a tender thrombosed lump at the anal margin.
describe: A bluish or purple tender swelling is visible at the edge of the anus.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Hallux valgus
key: Recognise **lateral deviation of the great toe** with a prominent medial first-metatarsal head.
describe: The great toe angles toward the lesser toes beside a prominent bunion.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Hammer toe
key: Look for a **fixed flexion deformity at the proximal interphalangeal joint** of a toe.
describe: One or more toes bend downward at the middle joint, often with a raised knuckle.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Achilles tendon rupture
key: Look for a **gap or loss of contour in the Achilles tendon**, with swelling above the heel.
describe: The tendon outline above the heel appears interrupted or swollen compared with the other side.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Clavicle fracture
key: Recognise **visible deformity or a step in the clavicle**, often with bruising and shoulder droop.
describe: The collarbone has an obvious bump or angulation, with the shoulder appearing lowered.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Colles fracture
key: Identify the **dinner-fork deformity** of the wrist caused by dorsal displacement of the distal radius.
describe: The wrist is swollen and bent backward, creating a characteristic fork-like profile.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Anterior shoulder dislocation
key: Look for a **squared-off shoulder contour** and prominent acromion with the arm held slightly away from the body.
describe: The shoulder loses its rounded contour, and the patient supports the affected arm.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Dupuytren contracture
key: Look for **thickened cords in the palm** pulling one or more fingers into fixed flexion.
describe: A palm with visible cords or nodules and a ring or little finger bent toward the palm.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Mallet finger
key: The **tip of the finger droops** at the distal joint and cannot be held straight.
describe: A finger with its end joint bent downward while the rest of the finger is relatively straight.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Boutonniere deformity
key: The finger has **middle-joint flexion with the fingertip joint extended**.
describe: A finger bent at its middle joint with the end joint held straight or slightly backward.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Swan-neck deformity
key: The finger shows **middle-joint hyperextension and fingertip-joint flexion**.
describe: A finger with a backward-bent middle joint and a bent fingertip.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Rheumatoid hand deformity
key: Recognise **multiple swollen joints and characteristic finger deviation or deformity**, often affecting both hands.
describe: Hands showing swollen knuckles and fingers angled toward the little-finger side, sometimes with other deformities.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Heberden nodes
key: Look for **firm bony swellings at the distal finger joints**, often on several fingers.
describe: One or more enlarged, knobbly joints close to the fingernails.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Cellulitis
key: The affected skin is **diffusely red, swollen, and poorly demarcated** compared with surrounding skin.
describe: An area of spreading redness and swelling, commonly on a lower leg.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Venous leg ulcer
key: A shallow ulcer near the **medial ankle**, often with surrounding brown pigmentation or venous skin changes.
describe: A shallow, irregular wound around the lower leg or ankle with discoloured surrounding skin.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Diabetic foot ulcer
key: Look for a **chronic ulcer on a pressure-bearing area of the foot**, often surrounded by callus.
describe: A wound on the sole or toe, sometimes with thickened callused skin around it.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Pressure ulcer
key: Recognise a **pressure injury over a bony prominence**, ranging from persistent non-blanching redness to deeper tissue loss.
describe: A pressure-related sore over the sacrum, heel, hip, or another prominent bone.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Lymphedema
key: Look for **persistent diffuse swelling of a limb**, often with thickened skin and involvement of the foot or hand.
describe: A markedly enlarged arm or leg with diffuse swelling and sometimes thickened skin.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Keloid
key: A **raised, firm scar extending beyond the original wound margins** is characteristic.
describe: A prominent, smooth raised scar that grows beyond the boundaries of the original injury.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Genu valgum
key: With the knees together, the **ankles remain separated**, producing an inward angulation of the legs.
describe: A standing person whose knees touch or nearly touch while the ankles are apart.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Genu varum
key: With the ankles together, the **knees remain separated**, producing outward bowing of the legs.
describe: A standing person with bowed legs and a visible gap between the knees.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Scoliosis
key: Look for **asymmetric shoulder or waist levels** and a sideways spinal curve, often clearer on forward bending.
describe: A person viewed from behind showing uneven shoulders or waist contours and a lateral spinal curve.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Multinodular goitre
key: Look for an enlarged, often nodular swelling at the front of the neck. It may rise when the patient swallows.
describe: A rounded or irregular swelling is visible over the lower front of the neck.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Gynecomastia
key: Recognise **enlarged male breast tissue**, often affecting both sides and centred beneath the nipples.
describe: One or both male breasts appear enlarged, sometimes with prominent areolae.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Breast cancer with peau d’orange
key: The key sign is breast skin with **pitting like orange peel**, often over an enlarged or distorted breast.
describe: A breast appears swollen or distorted, with visibly dimpled, orange-peel-like skin.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Rectal prolapse
key: Identify a **reddish protruding mass with concentric folds** emerging from the anus.
describe: Moist red rectal tissue protrudes through the anal opening.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Wet gangrene
key: Look for **swollen, discoloured tissue** with a moist appearance, often with blisters or discharge.
describe: An affected part, commonly a foot or toe, appears swollen and dark with damaged, moist tissue.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Polydactyly
key: Recognise a **supernumerary finger or toe** alongside the usual digits.
describe: A hand or foot has an extra digit, which may be fully formed or a small appendage.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Syndactyly
key: The distinguishing feature is **two or more digits joined by skin or tissue**.
describe: Adjacent fingers or toes appear webbed or fused together.
subject: Surgery & ortho

label: Open tibial fracture
key: Recognise a **visible wound over a deformed lower leg**, potentially exposing bone.
describe: The lower leg is visibly swollen or deformed, with an overlying wound near the fracture.
subject: Surgery & ortho
